title: Iterated conditioning on the special-bit event and fiber
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of its summary $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. The disjoint-conditioned hard-distribution measure, first further conditioned on Bob's special bit being false and then conditioned on $Z=z$, equals the disjoint-conditioned hard-distribution measure conditioned in one step on the intersection of those two events.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic length-$n$ disjointness protocol
replaced:
Fix an input length $n \ge 1$, a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of
length $n$, and an achievable value $z$ of the summary variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T},
Y_{>T})$. Let $D$ denote the hard distribution conditioned on the event that the two
generated input sets are disjoint, and write $Y_T$ for Bob's bit at the special
coordinate. Then conditioning $D$ first on the event $\{Y_T = \mathrm{false}\}$ and then
on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$ produces exactly the same measure as conditioning $D$ in a
single step on the intersection $\{Y_T = \mathrm{false}\} \cap \{Z = z\}$.
